typical_topologies: Point-to-point link: one master agent + one slave agent connected by a single link with 2 channels (A, D) for TL-UL/TL-UH, or 5 channels (A, B, C, D, E) for TL-C (Figure 2.1).
Hierarchical: master → crossbar → cache → memory controller, with both crossbar and cache having master + slave interfaces (Figure 2.2).
Crossbar module containing multiple agents — one routing agent + one config-access agent (Figure 2.3).
Example SoC: AXI bridge (read + write agents) → crossbar → clock-crossing → crossbar → SPI slave + SRAM + PCIe bridge (Figure 4.2).

interconnect_role.crossbar_routing: A TileLink crossbar is one TileLink agent with multiple master-side and multiple slave-side links. Messages received on any slave port may be forwarded to any master port — therefore all its ports belong to a single agent in the DAG.
interconnect_role.adapter_bridge: A TileLink-to-TileLink adapter (slave on one side, master on the other) is two independent agents inside one RTL module. Messages do not directly cross — they pass through an internal queue. Used for clock / power crossings.
interconnect_role.legacy_bus_bridge: A TileLink-to-{AXI,AHB,APB,PCIe} bridge is also two independent agents. The legacy-bus side must include timeouts to fit within forward-progress rule 1.
interconnect_role.address_decode: Per-link parameters and per-region address-map determine which slave receives a message. From any node in the DAG, every valid address routes over a single path to exactly one slave.
interconnect_role.configuration_agent: Crossbars or other interconnect modules may contain a second agent with a single slave interface providing access to configuration state.

interconnect_rules: Pairs of agents are connected by links. One end of each link connects to a master interface on one agent; the other connects to a slave interface on the other agent.
Any topology that can be described as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) is a legal topology.
Agents are graph vertices; links are graph edges directed from master interface to slave interface.
A single hardware module may contain multiple independent TileLink agents (e.g. a crossbar module can contain a routing agent and a configuration-access agent).

If two TileLink links connect to the same module but messages from one cannot result in recursive messages on the other without first passing through a third link, the module contains two distinct agents.
Both ends of a TileLink link must share the same clock / reset / power; cross-domain integration requires a TileLink-to-TileLink adapter.
It is forbidden for one side of a TileLink link to power down while its opposite is powered on.
deadlock_freedom_proof_sketch: 1. Agent graph is a DAG by construction.
2. Strict channel priority A < B < C < D < E enforced on every receiver.
3. Higher-priority messages may bypass lower-priority ones in transit.
4. Each receiver only lowers ready according to the 4 legitimate exceptions.
5. Combined, message flow through all channels between all agents remains acyclic, so no hold-and-wait loop is possible.
6. Therefore correct TileLink implementations are provably deadlock-free.

TL_UL.note: 12 signals = clock + reset + 7 channel-A control/data + 7 channel-D control/data (some shared widths).

TL_UH.note: Same as TL-UL but with bursts (size > log2(w)) and atomic param encodings used.

interfacing_with_legacy_buses: TileLink-to-AXI / TileLink-to-AHB / TileLink-to-APB / TileLink-to-PCIe bridges must include a timeout to fit within the first forward-progress rule.
If a legacy bus does not accept a request within the timeout, the bridge must discard the request and inject a TileLink error response.
If a legacy bus sends response messages and the response timeout fires, the bridge must cancel the outstanding request and inject a TileLink error response.
TileLink agents waiting on other TileLink agents must be infinitely patient (no timeouts inside the TileLink network itself).
address_space_recommendation: Recommend the address map not be a single global map — properties may change as messages move through the network.
Recommend address regions with Get/Put side effects be aligned to multiples of 4kB to ease TLB management.
Recommend the address map include an optional FIFO domain identifier annotating regions that mutually respond in FIFO order.
Slaves must declare maximum burst support; recommend at least 4kB minimum.
